chosen: Project skeleton governance: make the repository one-screen understandable and merge specs into the product repository.
why: The product loop is now proven, so the next bottleneck is maintainability: local artifacts, historical references, and a nested spec repository obscure the actual product surface.
changed_from: v0.12.0 stabilized local export resource usage.

constraints.no_vanity: The visible result is a clean root directory, current entry docs, and a structure gate that catches future drift.
constraints.no_overreach: This version governs repository skeleton, docs, spec ownership, and artifact boundaries; it does not rewrite editor/export business logic or reshape public CLI behavior.
constraints.no_rush: Archive before moving, preserve spec history as a bundle, and verify product build paths after the restructure.
constraints.must_verify: Acceptance is `find . -maxdepth 2`, structure checks, cargo/frontend checks, and a short desktop open smoke.

success_picture: A new engineer or AI opens the root and can immediately see code, frontend, examples, scripts, tests, and spec without tmp/reference/episodes noise.
cost_estimate: AI scale: 2-4 hours for migration, docs, checks, and lightweight verification.
risks: Nested spec git history can be lost if not bundled before removing spec/.git.
Accidentally tracking generated media or POC build artifacts would bloat the main repository.
Over-cleaning reference material could remove useful context, so local archive is required.

candidates.summary: Clean root layout, merge spec, archive local artifacts, add structure gate.
Reshape crates and frontend code boundaries after repository skeleton is stable.
Produce an audit report without moving files; rejected because the user asked to implement.
